questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to manage a heavy workload in the office
Why self-help books have become so popular
What resilience is and whether we can learn it
How young children learn best at school
questions.why: Rob says they're discussing whether we're born with resilience or have to learn it.

questions.q: How does Georgina show resilience at the start?
options: She stays calm despite a pile of work
She refuses to do extra work
She asks Rob for help
She takes the day off
questions.why: She says she has a pile of work but is remaining calm and not getting stressed.

questions.q: What is the first level of resilience Dr David Westley describes?
options: How much sleep we get
How optimistic we are
How we calm our nervous system
The social support around us
questions.why: He says first there's our social supports: communities, families and organisations.

questions.q: What do some experts think about people who ask for help?
options: They are less resilient than quiet people
They may be acting in a more resilient way
They are too dependent on others
They need professional therapy
questions.why: Rob says some experts think people who ask for help and use social support are more resilient.

questions.q: What is the biological level of resilience, according to Dr Westley?
options: How strong our muscles and bones are
Whether our parents and grandparents were resilient
How well we can calm ourselves down when upset
How healthy our diet is and how much we sleep
questions.why: He says it's how well we can soothe ourselves and regulate our nervous systems at times of distress.

questions.q: What did Professor Ann Masten find about resilience?
options: We are all born with the same amount
It is something we learn when we need to
It cannot be changed after childhood
Only adults can develop it
questions.why: Rob says she found it was something that we learn when we need to.

questions.q: Who are the 'late bloomers' in Ann Masten's studies?
options: Children who were resilient right from the start
Children who never managed to become resilient
Adults who went back to university to study psychology
Children who struggled at first but later coped well
questions.why: Rob says they started off less resilient, struggled, but turned their lives around.

questions.q: Why does Ann Masten say teachers and parents are important?
options: Children learn how to handle problems by watching them
They can protect children from all of life's problems
They decide how resilient a child is when it's born
They should tell children to toughen up and stop crying
questions.why: She says they're role models; children learn by seeing how adults react when challenged.
